Security & Compliance.title: What Zero Trust Actually Means
Security & Compliance.body:
Never assume trust, always verify. Zero Trust runs on three principles: verify explicitly, enforce least-privilege access, and assume breach. Verify confirms who or what is requesting access, least privilege grants only the permissions needed and only for as long as needed, and assume breach means you build proactive defenses as if your environment is already compromised.

▶ Full video: https://aka.ms/ZTMechanics

Security & Compliance.title: Your Image Scanner Can't See This Container Attack
Security & Compliance.body:
Image scanning won't catch a container that's been hijacked to mine crypto — because it's running something that was never in the original image. Containers should be immutable, so when Microsoft Defender for Cloud detects "binary drift" — a process the container was never built to run — it flags the runtime threat that scanning and posture alone can't see, down to the process, file, pod, and cluster.

Extending Tamper Protection, this capability locks settings to your defined values for consistent and predictable device states. For more information, see Controlled configuration for Microsoft Defender settings .

Endpoint & Device Management.title: Regional support for Microsoft Store apps
Endpoint & Device Management.body: Microsoft Intune now supports regional selection for Microsoft Store apps. When you add a Microsoft Store app, you can choose the region (market) whose Store catalog to search and deploy from. Previously, Intune searched only the United States catalog. Now you can deploy apps published for specific markets, such as Japan or Spain, that aren't available in the US catalog. For more information, see Add Microsoft Store apps to Microsoft Intune .

Identity & Access.title: Give Every AI Agent Its Own Identity
Identity & Access.body:
AI agents don't fall for phishing, but they're still vulnerable — they can be hijacked, and broad access means one misconfiguration can open the door to a major breach. The new Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives each AI agent its own unique, manageable identity, so you can apply the same visibility, governance, and Zero Trust controls you use for people to non-human actors too.

Identity & Access.body:
What actually is a session token, and why do attackers want it? Think of it like a theme-park pass: whoever holds it gets the rides — so if someone steals it after you sign in, they get your access without your password. 

Full explainer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gPcNlm0CyOw

Identity & Access.body:
MFA is essential — but is it enough? As more orgs turn on MFA, attackers pivot to credential-bypass attacks like token theft: Microsoft detected 147,000 token-theft attacks in a single year — a 111% jump — and the trend keeps climbing.

Note: The 147,000 / 111% figures are from the source video (2024) — accurate as stated, but this is illustrative of the trend, not this-year numbers.

AI & Copilot.title: Why Ungoverned AI Agents Are Dangerous
AI & Copilot.body:
Ungoverned AI agents are a new attack path. AI semantic search can surface information that was once hard to find and share it with the wrong people, and agents with extensive permissions can move through your organization at unparalleled speed — so if one is compromised, it can cause significant damage before anyone notices.
